definitions.explanation: Describes something that is wildly unrealistic, lacks any basis in fact, or is so far-fetched as to be ridiculous. A four-character compound ({四字熟語|よじじゅくご}) used to dismiss ideas, stories, or claims as groundless.

examples.japanese: {荒唐無稽|こうとうむけい}な{話|はなし}だ。
その{計画|けいかく}は{荒唐無稽|こうとうむけい}で、{誰|だれ}も{賛成|さんせい}しなかった。
examples.english: The plan was preposterous, and nobody agreed with it.

examples.japanese: {荒唐無稽|こうとうむけい}に{聞|き}こえるかもしれないが、{彼|かれ}の{提案|ていあん}には{一理|いちり}ある。
examples.english: It may sound preposterous, but there is some merit to his proposal.

notes:
USAGE:
This is a {四字熟語|よじじゅくご} (four-character compound). {荒唐|こうとう} means wild and unfounded, while {無稽|むけい} means without basis or evidence. Together they emphasize complete groundlessness.

Typically used as a na-adjective modifying nouns ({荒唐無稽|こうとうむけい}な{話|はなし}) or predicatively ({荒唐無稽|こうとうむけい}だ). It carries a strong dismissive tone.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {荒唐無稽|こうとうむけい}な{話|はなし} (absurd story)
- {荒唐無稽|こうとうむけい}な{主張|しゅちょう} (preposterous claim)
- {荒唐無稽|こうとうむけい}な{計画|けいかく} (absurd plan)
- {荒唐無稽|こうとうむけい}な{物語|ものがたり} (nonsensical tale)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ばかげた: ridiculous, silly (more colloquial)
- {馬鹿馬鹿|ばかばか}しい: absurd, stupid (stronger emotional dismissal)
- {無茶|むちゃ}: unreasonable, reckless (focuses on being impractical)
